mainTopic: The son of uncertain fatherhood in the משנה, and שמואל's rule that a child whose כהן father is unknown loses כהונה (only for זנות). The משנה is explained as a case of קידושי טעות.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a baby who could be the son of either of two men, because his mother remarried too soon. When one possible father is a כהן and the other a ישראל, he takes on the strict rules of both. When both are כהנים, mourning applies both ways, טומאה is forbidden both ways, and he serves with both משמרות. The גמרא first explains that חליצה must come before יבום for his widow. Then שמואל teaches that a child of one unknown man out of ten כהנים is a שתוקי and loses כהונה, because the פסוק requires 'his seed after him.' The גמרא limits this rule: it is דרבנן and applies only to זנות, not to marriage. A challenge from our משנה seems to refute שמואל, since the משנה lets the son serve as a כהן. רב שמעיא answers that the case is a ממאנת, but a young girl is not expected to give birth safely. So the גמרא settles on a woman whose קידושין were a mistake. Such a woman can be grown, can have a son, and can leave without a גט.

steps.title: Yibum with half-brothers from both possible fathers
steps.stepSummary: The son of doubtful fatherhood has half-brothers from each possible father. The משנה rules how יבום and חליצה work in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had brothers from the first husband and brothers from the second husband, not from the same mother: he performs חליצה and יבום. And with them, one does חליצה and one does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of rulings for the doubtful son. It now turns to brothers on both possible fathers' sides and the laws of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He might be a real brother to either set of brothers, but we don't know which. So the משנה uses a combination of חליצה and יבום that works whichever man is truly his father. When he dies childless, one brother from each side takes part: one does חליצה and the other does יבום. That way his widow is properly released no matter who the real father was.

keyTerms.meaning: performs חליצה, the ceremony that releases a childless widow from יבום
performs יבום, marrying the childless brother's widow
brothers from the first husband
not from the same mother, meaning only paternal half-brothers

steps.confusionAlert: These brothers are only paternal half-brothers from other wives. Since they share no mother with him, the doubt about who his father is decides whether they are brothers at all.

phrases.english: If he had brothers from the first husband
and brothers from the second husband,
not from the same mother —
he performs חליצה and יבום,
phrases.notes: This is about the widows of those brothers. Either way works: if he's not really their brother, she's just a woman he's allowed to marry.

phrases.english: and they — one performs חליצה and one performs יבום.
phrases.notes: This is about his own widow if he dies childless: one brother from each side takes part.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ לוֹ אַחִים מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן וְאַחִים מִן הַשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of rulings for the son of doubtful fatherhood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because his true brothers are unknown, יבום and חליצה are arranged so that they work whichever husband was the father.

steps.title: One possible father a Kohen: marriage and impurity
steps.stepSummary: If one possible father was a כהן and the other a ישראל, he must marry like a כהן and stay away from טומאת מת. But he gets no lashes if he becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one was a ישראל and one a כהן: he marries only a woman fit for a כהן, and he does not become impure from the dead. But if he did become impure, he does not receive the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new case: one possible father was a כהן. It starts with whom he may marry and the rules of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he might be a כהן, he must keep the כהן's restrictions as a safety measure. Lashes, though, need certainty that he broke a prohibition, and he might really be a ישראל. So he is not punished.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman fit to marry a כהן
becomes ritually impure through contact with the dead
receives the forty lashes, the punishment for breaking a לאו

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for the rest of the case: in a doubt he must be careful in practice, but he cannot be punished.

phrases.english: If one was a ישראל and one was a כהן —
he marries a woman fit for a כהן,
and he does not become impure for the dead.
And if he did become impure —
he does not receive the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the brothers case to a new case: the two possible fathers have different lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He keeps the כהן's marriage and טומאה restrictions, but he is not lashed for breaking them.

steps.title: Teruma rules for the doubtful Kohen
steps.stepSummary: He may not eat תרומה, but he doesn't pay if he did. He doesn't receive תרומה at the threshing floor, yet he may sell his own תרומה and keep the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not eat תרומה, and if he ate, he does not pay the principal and the fifth. He does not take a share at the threshing floor. He sells the תרומה, and the money is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same doubt to תרומה. It covers eating it, paying for it, receiving it, and selling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating is forbidden because he might be a ישראל. But a fine of קרן וחומש can't be collected because he might be a כהן. Others won't give him תרומה, since he can't prove he's a כהן. But his own תרומה can't be taken from him either, so he sells it to a real כהן and keeps the money.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of produce given to a כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it
the principal plus an added fifth, which a non-כהן pays for eating תרומה by mistake
takes a share of תרומה at the threshing floor
the money is his

phrases.english: He does not eat תרומה,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָכַל — אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וָחוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: and if he ate — he does not pay the principal and the fifth.
And he does not take a share at the threshing floor.
And he sells the תרומה, and the money is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the כהן/ישראל case, now applied to תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is barred from eating or receiving תרומה, but he cannot be made to pay, and his own תרומה stays his to sell.

steps.title: Sacrifices, priestly gifts, and his firstborn animal
steps.stepSummary: He gets no share of קדשים and isn't given offerings to bring, but what he holds stays his. He is exempt from the priestly gifts, and his בכור grazes until it gets a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not share in קדשי קדשים, and they do not give him קדשים, but they do not take what is his out of his hand. He is exempt from the foreleg, the jaw and the maw. And his firstborn animal grazes until it becomes blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing rules for the doubtful כהן, now covering קרבנות and gifts owed to a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same logic: he can't claim כהן rights, so he gets no share of offerings. But no one can take from him without proof, so what he holds stays his. A real ישראל would give the gifts to a כהן, but no כהן can prove he is owed them by this man. His בכור can't be given away or eaten unblemished, so it waits until a blemish lets him eat it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: the most holy offerings, eaten only by male כהנים
the foreleg, jaw and maw, which are given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal
a firstborn male animal, normally given to a כהן
until it becomes blemished and unfit as an offering

phrases.english: And he does not take a share of the most holy offerings.
And they do not give him the consecrated offerings,
but they do not take what is his out of his hand.
And he is exempt from the foreleg, the jaw and the maw.
And his firstborn animal should graze until it becomes blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the תרומה pattern to קדשים, the priestly gifts, and בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He gets no כהן privileges from others, yet nothing can be taken from him or demanded of him, because he might be a כהן.

steps.title: The general rule: stringencies of both
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up the whole כהן/ישראל case: he carries the strict rules of כהנים and the strict rules of ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we place upon him the stringencies of כהנים and the stringencies of ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes the כהן/ישראל case with one rule that explains everything listed before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every earlier ruling fits this rule. Where being a כהן would restrict him (marriage, טומאה), he is restricted. Where being a ישראל would restrict him (תרומה, קדשים), he is restricted too. The leniencies, like no lashes, no payment, and keeping what he holds, come from the fact that no one can prove his status against him.

keyTerms.meaning: the stringencies that apply to כהנים
the stringencies that apply to ישראלים

steps.whatToRemember: When it is unclear whether someone is a כהן, he gets the strict side of both statuses. But punishments and money claims that need proof are not imposed on him.

phrases.english: And we place upon him the stringencies of priests
and the stringencies of Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חוּמְרֵי כֹּהֲנִים וְחוּמְרֵי יִשְׂרְאֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes the list of rulings in steps 2 through 4 under one principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A doubtful כהן takes on the stringencies of both כהנים and ישראלים.

steps.title: Both possible fathers Kohanim: mourning, impurity, inheritance
steps.stepSummary: If both possible fathers were כהנים, he mourns for both and they mourn for him. No one may become טמא for the other, and they inherit from him, but he does not inherit from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both were כהנים: he is an אונן over them, and they are אוננים over him. He does not become impure for them, and they do not become impure for him. He does not inherit them, but they inherit him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to its last case: both possible fathers were כהנים. Now he is surely a כהן, and the only doubt is which man is his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mourning (אנינות) is a stringency, so it applies to each man in case he is the real father. Becoming טמא is only allowed for a definite close relative, so it is forbidden on both sides. He can't inherit, because each family's heirs can say "prove he's ours." But they inherit from him, since one of them is surely his father and they share the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: a mourner in the first stage of grief, before burial, with special restrictions
becomes impure for them, which a כהן may do only for close relatives
inherits

steps.confusionAlert: Inheritance goes only one way. He can't take from either estate because each set of heirs can push him off. But when he dies, both possible fathers together certainly include his real father, so they inherit from him.
steps.whatToRemember: With two possible כהן fathers, the stringencies (mourning, no טומאה) apply both ways. Inheritance goes only to them, because only they can be sure one of them is the right heir.

phrases.english: If both of them were priests —
he is an acute mourner over them,
and they are acute mourners over him.
He does not become impure for them,
and they do not become impure for him.
He does not inherit from them,
but they inherit from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the mixed כהן/ישראל case to the case where both possible fathers are כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mourning applies both ways, טומאה is forbidden both ways, and inheritance flows only from him to them.

steps.title: No punishment for hitting or cursing either possible father
steps.stepSummary: The son of two possible כהנים fathers is exempt from punishment for striking or cursing either of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is exempt for hitting or cursing either one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues listing the rules for the son whose father is either one of two כהנים. It now says he cannot be punished for hitting or cursing either man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting or cursing a parent normally carries the death penalty. Here we cannot say for sure about either man that he is the father, so neither act can be punished.

keyTerms.meaning: Hitting him (here, a possible father)
Cursing him
Exempt from punishment

phrases.english: And he is exempt for hitting him and for cursing him
of this one and of that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rules from step 6 for the case of two כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no punishment for striking or cursing either possible father.

steps.title: Serving with the priestly watches and sharing in the offerings
steps.stepSummary: He serves with the watch of each possible father but gets no share. If both men are in the same watch, he gets one share.
steps.simpleTranslation: He goes up to serve with the watch of each one, but he does not take a share. If both were in one watch, he takes one share.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on how this son takes part in the בית המקדש service. It explains when he gets a portion of the offerings and when he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He really does belong to one of the two watches, so he must serve with both. Each watch can push him off to the other one, so he ends up with no share. When both men are in the same watch, that watch is surely his, so he takes one share.

keyTerms.meaning: A priestly watch, a group of כהנים that takes its turn serving in the בית המקדש
Takes a share (of the offerings)
Receives a portion

steps.whatToRemember: The son of two possible כהנים fathers carries the duties of both. He only gets benefits where his claim is certain, as when both men are in one watch.

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלֶה בְּמִשְׁמָרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה וְשֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: He goes up to serve with the watch of this one and of that one,
but he does not take a share.
If both of them were in one watch —
he takes one share.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלֶה בְּמִשְׁמָרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה וְשֶׁל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last rules of the משנה for the two-כהנים case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He serves with both watches and takes no share. If both possible fathers share one watch, he takes one share.

steps.title: חליצה must come first, then יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that in the משנה's case of half-brothers, one brother must do חליצה first, and only then may the other do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Specifically, first חליצה and afterward יבום. But יבום first, no, because he would run into the prohibition of a יבמה marrying an outsider.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining an earlier line of the משנה. When this uncertain son dies without children, one half-brother does חליצה and the other does יבום. The order matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half-brother might not be the real brother. If one did יבום first, he might be an outsider living with a יבמה who is still bound to the real brother, and that is forbidden. Doing חליצה first frees her from either possible brother, so the יבום that follows is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Specifically, only this way
To perform חליצה
To perform יבום
A יבמה with an outsider (someone who is not her יבם), which is forbidden

phrases.english: GEMARA: Specifically, first doing חליצה
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier line in the משנה, where one half-brother does חליצה and the other does יבום.

phrases.english: and afterward doing יבום,
but doing יבום first — no,
because he would run into the prohibition of a יבמה with an outsider.
phrases.notes: Literally "to the marketplace." He means any man who is not her יבם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by clarifying an earlier clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה must come before יבום, so that no one does יבום with a יבמה who may not be his.

steps.title: שמואל: a child of one of ten כהנים is a שתוקי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if one unknown man from a group of ten כהנים had relations with a woman, her child is a שתוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Ten כהנים are standing, one of them left and had relations. The child is a שתוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from שמואל. It deals with a child whose father is surely a כהן, but we cannot tell which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the משנה's case of two known possible fathers, here the father is one unknown man out of ten. שמואל gives the child the label שתוקי, and the next steps explain what that label means.

keyTerms.meaning: Separated from the group, went off
A "silenced one": a child whose father is not known

phrases.english: שמואל said:
Ten כהנים are standing together,
and one of them went off and had relations with a woman —
the child is a שתוקי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, related in theme to the uncertain-father case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child fathered by an unidentified one of ten כהנים is called a שתוקי.

steps.title: What does שתוקי mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל means by calling the child a שתוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "שתוקי" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the label שתוקי means in שמואל's case. This sets up the next two steps, which give a wrong answer and then the right one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word means "silenced," but silenced from what? The גמרא wants to find the practical result of this label.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: What does "שתוקי" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of שמואל's term.

steps.title: Not about inheritance, since that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers that שתוקי means he cannot inherit his father, then rejects it because that is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they silence him from his father's property, that is obvious! Do we even know who his father is?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning, losing his father's inheritance, and throws it out. שמואל would not need to teach something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody knows which of the ten men is his father, so of course he cannot claim any one man's property. A teaching must add something new, so this cannot be what שמואל meant.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
It's obvious!
His father's property

phrases.english: If you say that they silence him
from his father's property —
that's obvious!
Do we even know who his father is?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading שתוקי as only losing inheritance.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That result is obvious, since the father is unknown, so שמואל would not need to say it.

steps.title: He is silenced from the status of כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שתוקי means the child does not get the status of a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they silence him from the status of כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of שמואל's term: the child is not treated as a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the new point. Every one of the ten men is a כהן, so his father is surely a כהן. Even so, the child does not receive כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (bringing the correct answer)
The legal status of a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that the doubt is whether the father was a כהן. All ten were כהנים, and the child still loses כהונה.

phrases.english: Rather, they silence him
from the status of כהונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שתוקי means he loses the status of כהונה, even though his father is surely a כהן.

steps.title: Why does he lose כהונה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the child is not a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a child whose father is surely a כהן should lose כהונה. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic would seem to say he is a כהן no matter which man is his father. The גמרא therefore needs a source for taking his כהונה away.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the ruling of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for denying כהונה when the father is surely a כהן.

steps.title: The פסוק requires offspring traced to the father
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "to him and to his seed after him" teaches that a כהן's offspring must be traceable to him, and this child is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And it shall be to him and to his seed after him." We need his offspring to be traced after him, and that is missing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It shows that כהונה passes only to children whose lineage is known to come from a specific כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "his seed after him" mean the child must be linked to a particular father. Here no one can tell which man is the father, so that condition is missing and כהונה does not pass down.

keyTerms.meaning: His offspring
Traced in lineage to a specific father
And it is not there

steps.whatToRemember: A שתוקי from one of ten כהנים is not a כהן. The reason is not doubt about כהונה; כהונה needs offspring clearly traced to one specific כהן ("לו ולזרעו אחריו").
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule: כהונה is passed down through known lineage, not just through being surely born from some כהן.

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
"And it shall be to him and to his seed after him,"
we need his offspring to be traced in lineage after him,
and here that is missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְהָיְתָה לּוֹ וּלְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "ולזרעו אחריו" requires offspring traced to a specific כהן, which this child is not.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about the same phrase said to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges the reading of 'his seed after him' by asking what the identical phrase means in אברהם's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: If so, look at אברהם, where it says 'To be a God to you and to your seed after you.' What is God warning him about there?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the explanation from step 15 by pointing to a פסוק about אברהם that uses the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'his seed after him' means the child must be traceable to the father, the same words in אברהם's פסוק would seem to mean the same thing. But it is unclear what such a warning would mean for אברהם, so the explanation looks shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: strongly objects
but if so (if your reasoning is right)
warns
the Merciful One (God, the Torah)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objects to this:
But if so, regarding Abraham,
where it is written: "To be a God to you
and to your seed after you,"

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם מַאי קָא מַזְהַר לֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא?
phrases.english: there, what is the Merciful One warning him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation from the פסוק given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'his seed after him' as requiring traceable lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same phrase said to אברהם does not seem to fit that meaning, so the reading needs explaining.

steps.title: The phrase to אברהם warns against marrying a non-Jew or maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק to אברהם means: do not marry a גויה or a שפחה, because the child would follow the mother's status.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what God told him: Don't marry a non-Jewish woman or a maidservant, so your children won't follow her status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא by explaining what 'your seed after you' means for אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אברהם, 'your seed after you' means his children should count as his. If he married a גויה or שפחה, the child would take her status, not his. So the phrase still fits the idea that offspring must follow the father.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jewish woman
a maidservant (slave woman)
will follow her (take her status)

phrases.english: This is what He said to him:
Do not marry a gentile woman or a maidservant,
so that your offspring will not follow her.
phrases.notes: The child of such a woman takes her status, so he would not count as אברהם's child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the parallel פסוק so it fits the same idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase to אברהם makes no sense under the lineage reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: For אברהם it warns against a marriage where the child follows the mother's status.

steps.title: A ברייתא lets an uncertain first son become a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא saying the 'first' son, whose father is uncertain, may become a כהן גדול, which contradicts the traceable-lineage rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: The ברייתא says the first son is fit to be a כהן גדול. But we need his offspring to be traceable to him, and here that is missing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go against the rule that a כהן's child must be traceable to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, a כהן married his brother's widow too soon after his death, so the first son could be from either brother. Even so, the ברייתא allows that son to be a כהן גדול, though his father is not known for sure.

keyTerms.meaning: High Priest
his offspring is traced to him

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The first is fit to be a High Priest.
But don't we require his offspring traced to him,
and that is missing!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: רִאשׁוֹן רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the rule from steps 13–15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a child whose father is unknown is not a כהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives full כהונה, even כהן גדול, to a son with an uncertain father.

steps.title: The traceable-lineage rule is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The requirement of זרעו מיוחס אחריו is דרבנן, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that his offspring must be traceable to him is rabbinic, and the verse is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by lowering the rule from Torah law to a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah itself does not require traceable lineage, the רבנן could decide where their rule applies. The פסוק is only a hint they leaned on, not the real source. This opens room for the ברייתא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic law (not from the Torah)
a verse used only as a support for a rabbinic rule
merely, just

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is throwing out the פסוק from step 15. It keeps the פסוק, but only as a hint for a rule the רבנן made.

phrases.english: His offspring traced to him is rabbinic,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First part of the answer to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the rule's source as rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lineage rule is from the Torah and applies everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is rabbinic, so its scope can be limited.

steps.title: The rabbinic rule applies only to זנות, not to marriage
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made the rule only for a child born from זנות; in a case of marriage, like the ברייתא's, they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the רבנן made this rule, it was for promiscuous relations. In a marriage, the רבנן did not make the rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by limiting the rabbinic rule to זנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case is a real marriage (יבום), so the rule does not apply and the son can be a כהן גדול. שמואל's case from earlier steps involves זנות, so there the child is not a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: decreed
promiscuous (non-marital) relations
marriage

steps.whatToRemember: Traceable lineage for a כהן is a rabbinic rule, and the רבנן applied it only to children born from זנות, not from marriage.

phrases.english: And when the Rabbis decreed, it was regarding promiscuity;
regarding marriage the Rabbis did not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's uncertain son should not be a כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic rule does not cover marriage, so the ברייתא stands.

steps.title: Did the רבנן really make the rule even for זנות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether the rule applies to זנות, starting to bring a משנה about a woman who remarried within three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did the רבנן really make the rule for promiscuity? Didn't we learn in a משנה: A woman who did not wait three months after her husband, then married and gave birth...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 20 and starts quoting a משנה. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא examines that משנה to build its challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the rule applies only to זנות. Now the גמרא asks whether it applies even to זנות, using a משנה about a child whose father is uncertain. To use the משנה, the גמרא first needs to figure out what case it is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: waited
three months

phrases.english: And regarding promiscuity, did the Rabbis decree?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁהֲתָה אַחַר בַּעְלָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
phrases.english: A woman who did not wait three months after her husband
and married and gave birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction drawn in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן made the lineage rule for זנות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about an uncertain child will be used to question whether the rule applies even to זנות.

steps.title: What does 'after her husband' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'after her husband' and suggests it means after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'after her husband' mean? If you say it means after her husband's death...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the משנה is describing and offers a first guess: the husband died. This sets up a test of that guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To use the משנה, the גמרא must know whether the first marriage ended by death or some other way. It starts with the simplest reading, death, and will check it against the end of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: after her husband
if you say
the death of

phrases.english: What is "after her husband"?
If you say after her husband's death,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the משנה just cited in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'after her husband' means after his death or something else.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A first suggestion: after his death (tested in the next step).

steps.title: The משנה's ending doesn't fit a husband who died
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says the fathers mourn the son, which can't happen if the first husband was already dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: He is an אונן over them, and they are אוננים over him. 'He is an אונן over them' works: when the second husband dies, and when the bones of the first husband are gathered. But 'they are אוננים over him' — how can that be? The first husband is already dead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the 'death' reading against the end of the משנה and shows it doesn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son could mourn both possible fathers: the second when he dies, and the first when his bones are reburied. But the משנה also says both men mourn the son, which is impossible if the first husband died before the son was born. So 'after her husband' can't mean after his death.

keyTerms.meaning: a mourner in the first, most intense stage of mourning
say the last part (of the משנה)
granted, this part works
gathering a dead person's bones for reburial

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
He is an onen over them,
phrases.notes: "He" is the son and "them" are the two possible fathers.

phrases.english: and they are onenim over him.
Granted, "he is an onen over them":
you find it with the marriage of the second
and the gathering of the bones of the first.
phrases.notes: When a buried person's bones are moved for reburial, the relatives mourn again, so the son can mourn the first husband this way.

phrases.english: But "they are onenim over him":
how can you find it?
The first is already dead!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and undermines the suggestion from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'after her husband' means after his death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's ending has both possible fathers mourning the son, which a dead first husband cannot do.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה is about a גרושה, and 'after her husband' means after her husband's גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say the משנה is about a divorced woman. 'After her husband' means after she got a גט from her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'after her husband' can't mean after he died (step 23), the גמרא tries a new reading: after he divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first husband only divorced her, he is still alive, so both men can mourn the son as the end of the משנה says. This fixes the problem raised in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman
A divorce document

phrases.english: Rather, it is about a divorced woman,
and what does 'after her husband' mean?
After her husband's divorce document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading to escape the problem in step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'After her husband' meant after his death
steps.terutzMaskana: 'After her husband' means after he divorced her

steps.title: The son not becoming impure for the fathers doesn't fit a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says the son does not become impure for either father. That is hard to explain if the mother was a גרושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: he does not become impure for them, and they do not become impure for him. It makes sense that they don't become impure for him, as a stringency, since for each one, maybe he is not his son. But why doesn't he become impure for them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the divorcée reading using the end of the משנה, which says the son may not become impure to bury either father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fathers holding back makes sense, since each might not really be the father. But the son holding back is puzzling. The next step explains exactly why.

keyTerms.meaning: The end clause of a משנה
Becomes ritually impure (here, by burying a dead person)
As a stringency

phrases.english: Say the end clause:
He does not become impure for them,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the son, and 'them' are the two men who might be his father.

phrases.english: and they do not become impure for him.
It makes sense that they do not become impure for him,
as a stringency,
since for each and every one,
maybe he is not his son.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הוּא אֵין מִטַּמֵּא לָהֶם, אַמַּאי?
phrases.english: But he does not become impure for them, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the divorcée reading
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה is about a גרושה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא's rule that the son can't become impure for his fathers doesn't fit that case

steps.title: For the first husband, the son should be allowed either way
steps.stepSummary: The son could become impure for the first husband no matter who his father is: either it is his real father, or the son is a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he shouldn't become impure for the second husband. But for the first, he should be allowed either way. If he is his son, he may properly become impure for him. And if he is the later husband's son, he may also properly become impure for him, because he is a חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the son's rule is a problem: for the first husband, both possibilities lead to permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who marries a גרושה has children who are חללים, and a חלל has no כהונה restrictions about טומאה. So if the son belongs to the second husband, he is a חלל and may become impure for anyone. If he belongs to the first husband, it is his own father. Either way he should be allowed for the first husband, so the משנה can't be about a גרושה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it
A child of a כהן from a forbidden union; disqualified from כהונה
Properly, fine

phrases.english: It makes sense that for the second husband
he should not become impure for him,
but for the first he should become impure for him
whichever way you look at it!
If he is his son,
he properly becomes impure for him,
and if he is the son of the later one,
he properly becomes impure for him,
since he is a חלל.
phrases.notes: The second husband is a כהן who married a divorcée, so his son would lose כהונה status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the question in step 25
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ממה נפשך argument shows that the son should be permitted to become impure for the first husband

steps.title: So the משנה must be about זנות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the משנה is about זנות, reading 'בעלה' (her husband) as 'בועלה' (the man she was with).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it about זנות? And 'after her husband' means after the man she had relations with.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out death and divorce, the גמרא concludes the case must be זנות. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unmarried woman was with one man and then married a כהן within three months, so the father is unknown. No גט is involved, so the son is not a חלל, and the problem from step 26 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Relations outside of marriage
The man who had relations with her

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it about זנות?
And what does 'after her husband' mean?
After the man she had relations with.
phrases.notes: A small play on letters: בעלה (her husband) is read as בועלה (the man she was with).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed divorcée reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was about a divorcée

steps.title: The son serves in both משמרות, which refutes שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says the son serves with either father's משמר. In a זנות case, that contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the end clause teaches: he goes up to serve in the משמר of this one and of that one. This is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the case is זנות, the גמרא points out that the משנה lets this son serve as a כהן. That seems to refute שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19-20 said the rule of זרעו מיוחס אחריו (lineage must be clear) is דרבנן and applies to a child from זנות. Here, in a זנות case with an unknown father, the משנה lets him serve anyway, so שמואל's position seems refuted. This finishes the challenge that began in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: A rotation shift of כהנים in the בית המקדש
Goes up (to serve)
A refutation

phrases.english: And the end clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלֶה בְּמִשְׁמָר שֶׁל זֶה וְשֶׁל זֶה.
phrases.english: He goes up in the משמר of this one and of that one.
This is a refutation of שמואל!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the זנות reading to complete the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule as defended in steps 19-20
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The child of זנות with unclear lineage serves in the משמר, against the rule that lineage must be clear

steps.title: The case is a girl who refused her husband
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיא answers that the משנה is about a ממאנת. That is a marriage, not זנות, and not a divorce either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיא said: It is about a girl who refused her husband (a ממאנת).
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיא saves שמואל by finding a case that is neither divorce nor זנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor girl married off by her brothers can cancel the marriage with מיאון. That cancels it completely, so she is not a גרושה and the son of the second כהן is not a חלל, which fixes step 26. Since it was a real marriage and not זנות, the rabbinic rule from step 20 does not apply, so he may serve.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl who refuses and cancels her marriage
Refusal that cancels a minor's marriage

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can't be about a widow (step 23), a divorcée (step 26), or זנות (step 28, against שמואל). רב שמעיא suggests a ממאנת: a real marriage with no גט. The next step challenges this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer would save שמואל's rule for זנות, but the next step challenges it, and the גמרא then gives a different case (step 31).

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said:
It is about a girl who refused her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of שמואל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only remaining option was זנות, which refutes שמואל
steps.terutzMaskana: A ממאנת case: marriage without a גט, so no חלל and no זנות

steps.title: Can a girl who does מיאון even have a baby?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שמעיא from a ברייתא. It shows that pregnancy at the age of מיאון is treated as dangerous, so the case is very unlikely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a ממאנת give birth? But רב ביבי taught before רב נחמן: three women may use a מוך (a contraceptive absorbent). They are a קטנה, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman. A קטנה may use it because she might get pregnant and die. A pregnant woman may use it because her unborn baby might be crushed into a 'sandal'. A nursing woman may use it because she might have to wean her baby early, and the baby could die. Who counts as a קטנה? A girl from eleven years and one day until twelve years and one day. Younger or older than that, she lives with her husband in the normal way. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: all of them live with their husbands in the normal way, and Heaven will have mercy, as the פסוק says, 'ה׳ protects the simple.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב שמעיא's answer. A girl young enough to do מיאון is not expected to have a baby safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון only applies to a girl who is still a קטנה. The ברייתא shows that a קטנה who gets pregnant is in danger of dying, so she is not expected to give birth. The חכמים disagree about using a מוך, but they still rely on Heaven's mercy, so even they treat pregnancy for her as risky. That makes it hard to say the משנה, which talks about a son being born, is about a ממאנת.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl married off as a minor who refuses the marriage (מיאון) and leaves without a גט
A soft absorbent material used to prevent pregnancy
A girl who is still a minor
A pregnant woman
A nursing mother
'ה׳ protects the simple': Heaven guards people who cannot protect themselves

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים. The גמרא only needs the part they both accept: a קטנה is not expected to become pregnant and give birth safely.

phrases.english: Does a girl who refuses her husband give birth?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Beivai teach before Rav Naḥman:
Three women may have relations using a contraceptive absorbent:
a minor girl, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman.
A minor girl, because she might become pregnant and die;
a pregnant woman, because her fetus might become a 'sandal';
phrases.notes: A 'sandal' means a fetus crushed flat, like the sole of a shoe, if a second pregnancy starts.

phrases.aramaic: מְנִיקָה — שֶׁמָּא תִּגְמוֹל אֶת בְּנָהּ וְיָמוּת.
phrases.english: a nursing woman, because she might have to wean her child and he would die.
And who is a minor girl here?

phrases.aramaic: מִבַּת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: From the age of eleven years and one day

phrases.aramaic: עַד בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: until the age of twelve years and one day.

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִיכֵּן אוֹ יָתֵר עַל כֵּן —
phrases.english: Younger than this or older than this,
she goes ahead and has relations in her normal way.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
Both this one and that one
go ahead and have relations in the normal way,
and Heaven will have mercy.
As it says: 'The Lord protects the simple'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְמָאֶנֶת מִי קָא יָלְדָה? וְהָתָנֵי רַב בִּיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שמעיא's answer from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמעיא's claim that the משנה is about a ממאנת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a קטנה can do מיאון, and a ברייתא treats pregnancy for a קטנה as life-threatening. So she is not expected to give birth, yet the משנה is about a son being born.

steps.title: The case is a mistaken betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can be about a woman whose קידושין were a mistake, following רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can find this case with a mistaken betrothal, following what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case that fits the משנה: a woman whose קידושין were a mistake. It then points to a teaching of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קידושי טעות, the marriage falls away without a divorce. So she is not a גרושה and may marry a כהן. She can also be an adult, so having a baby is no problem. This avoids every earlier difficulty: it is not a divorce, it is not זנות, and it is not a young girl.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal made by mistake, which falls away without a גט
'You can find it': here is a case where it works

phrases.english: You can find it with a mistaken betrothal,
following what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30 by changing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'refusing' woman had to be a young girl, who cannot safely give birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a woman with קידושי טעות. She can be an adult, she is not a גרושה, and her marriage is not זנות.

steps.title: שמואל's teaching: a coerced סוטה stays permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל in the name of רבי ישמעאל. The פסוק about a סוטה shows that a woman who was forced stays permitted to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי ישמעאל: 'And she was not forced' means she is forbidden. If she was forced, she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the teaching it pointed to in the last step. This first part sets up the basic rule from the פסוק about a סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a סוטה becomes forbidden when 'she was not forced.' From this we learn that if she was forced, she stays permitted to her husband. This is the base. The next step uses the extra word 'she' to add another case.

keyTerms.meaning: She was seized or forced
Forbidden / permitted to her husband

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel
in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
'And she was not forced': then she is forbidden,
so if she was forced, she is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching that step 31 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the משנה is about קידושי טעות
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי ישמעאל, explaining the סוטה פסוק

steps.title: A mistaken-betrothal wife can walk away even after having a child
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'she' teaches about another woman who stays permitted even though she was not forced: a woman with קידושי טעות. She can leave even after having a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is another woman who stays permitted even though she was not forced. Who is she? A woman whose קידושין were a mistake. Even with her son riding on her shoulders, she can refuse and walk away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes שמואל's teaching. It shows that a woman with קידושי טעות can leave even after having a child, so she fits the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman with קידושי טעות was never truly married, so being with another man does not make her forbidden. The words 'her son on her shoulders' show that such a woman can already have children and still leave. That is exactly what the משנה needs: a real, grown woman with a son, who is free of her first husband without a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Riding on her shoulders
She refuses and goes on her way

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: the משנה is not about a young girl doing מיאון. It is about a woman whose קידושין were a mistake. She can be grown, she can have children, and she leaves without a גט, so she is not a גרושה.
steps.confusionAlert: The word ממאנת here does not mean the formal מיאון of a young girl. It just means she can reject the marriage and leave, because it was never valid.

phrases.english: And you have another woman,
phrases.notes: The extra word 'she' (וְהִיא) in the פסוק is what hints at this other woman.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּשָׂה, מוּתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: who, even though she was not forced, is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵי זוֹ — זוֹ שֶׁקִּדּוּשֶׁיהָ קִידּוּשֵׁי טָעוּת,
phrases.english: And who is she? The one whose betrothal was a mistaken betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בְּנָהּ מוּרְכָּב לָהּ עַל כְּתֵפָהּ —
phrases.english: so that even if her son is riding on her shoulders,
she refuses and goes on her way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ לְךָ אַחֶרֶת, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּשָׂה, מוּתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's teaching from step 32 and applies it to the answer in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman with קידושי טעות can have a child and still leave without a גט
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word 'וְהִיא' in the סוטה פסוק, as taught by שמואל in the name of רבי ישמעאל
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the משנה's case can really happen: a grown woman with a son leaves her first husband without a divorce, so she may marry a כהן.
